title: The Shus Endings
kidRule: A 'shus' ending is spelled C-I-O-U-S or T-I-O-U-S. To pick the right one, think of a word in the same family: SPACE has a C, so it is SPACIOUS. CAUTION has a T, so it is CAUTIOUS.
hint: Listen to the 'shus' at the end. There is no S-H in it! Is it C-I-O-U-S or T-I-O-U-S? Think of a word from the same family to help you choose.
reminder: The 'shus' ending is C-I-O-U-S or T-I-O-U-S. If your first try did not work, try the other!

check.question: Why does CAUTIOUS end with T-I-O-U-S?
check.correctAnswer: The 'shus' ending is C-I-O-U-S or T-I-O-U-S, and CAUTION already has a T!
distractors: Because 'shus' is always spelled with S-H
Because every describing word has to have a T in it

words.def: Tasting or smelling very, very good.
words.sent: Grandpa baked a delicious apple pie.
words.story: Your tongue has thousands of tiny taste buds. They are what tell you when a bite is delicious!
words.card: The *deli* made a *delicious* sandwich as tall as a giraffe!

words.def: Taking care so that nothing goes wrong.
words.sent: The cautious kitten sniffed the water before stepping in.
words.story: Meerkats are cautious animals. While the family digs for food, one meerkat stands tall on its back legs and keeps watch!
words.card: The *cautious* dinos*au*r tiptoed past the sleeping kitten!

words.def: Worth a lot, or loved very much.
words.sent: My precious teddy bear sleeps beside my pillow.
words.story: This word comes from the Latin word 'pretium', which means price. The word PRICE comes from it too!
words.card: My *precious* *pre*tzel has its own tiny pillow!

words.sent: Our tent was spacious enough for the whole family.
words.story: The International Space Station is surprisingly spacious. It has more room to live in than a six-bedroom house!
words.card: The hippo's *spa* was so *spacious* that ten ducks came for a bath!

words.def: Wanting very much to do big things, and ready to work hard for them.
words.sent: The ambitious builder planned a sandcastle taller than herself.
words.story: This word comes from a Latin word for 'going around'. In ancient Rome, people who wanted to be leaders walked around the city asking for votes!
words.card: The *ambitious* rab*bit* planned to hop all the way to the moon!

words.def: Feeling that something is not quite right.
words.sent: Mom was suspicious when the cookie jar was empty.
words.story: This word comes from a Latin word that means to look up at something from below, the way you might peek at someone you are not sure about!
words.card: The *suspicious* squirrel checked the *pic*nic basket for hidden acorns!

words.def: Kind, polite, and pleasant to others.
words.sent: The gracious host thanked every guest for coming.
words.story: This word comes from the Latin word 'gratia'. So does 'gracias', the Spanish word for thank you!
words.card: The *gracious* *rac*coon said thank you for every single crumb!

words.sent: My kitten thinks she is a ferocious tiger.
words.story: Tyrannosaurus rex looked ferocious, but its arms were tiny: only about three feet long!
words.card: The *ferocious* hamster roared from the top of the *fer*ris wheel!

words.def: Full of the good things your body needs to grow and stay healthy.
words.sent: A nutritious breakfast gives you energy for the morning.
words.story: Carrots are nutritious. Your body turns the orange color inside them into vitamin A, which helps keep your eyes healthy!
words.card: The squirrel packed a *nutritious* *nut* sandwich for lunch!

words.def: Awake and able to notice what is going on around you.
words.sent: I was conscious of a tiny tickle on my toe.
words.story: This word comes from Latin words that mean 'knowing with'. The S-C-I in the middle means 'know', just as it does in SCIENCE!
words.card: I was *conscious* that my *sci*ence project was bubbling over!
